title: Proper morphisms and etale-origin torsion sheaves satisfy the ph comparison hypotheses
statement:
Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes and compatible small site presentations as in [def-weil-size-convention]. On the category $\mathcal C=\mathrm{Sch}/S$ use the big etale topology and the big ph topology [def-trf-ph-scheme-site]. For $X\in\mathcal C$, write $B_X=(\mathrm{Sch}/X)_{\mathrm{Et}}$, $P_X=(\mathrm{Sch}/X)_{ph}$, and let $\pi_X:\mathrm{Sh}(B_X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{Et}})$ be the big-to-small etale morphism of [lem-trf-big-small-etale-exact-retraction]. The etale topology is coarser than the ph topology. Write $\epsilon_X:\mathrm{Sh}(P_X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(B_X)$ for the comparison geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism] induced by the identity, with direct image the identity on underlying presheaves and inverse image ph sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ induces the relocalization morphism $f_{\mathrm{Et}}:\mathrm{Sh}(B_X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(B_Y)$, whose inverse image sends $H$ to the sheaf $(U\to X)\mapsto H(U\to X\to Y)$. Write $R^if_{\mathrm{Et},*}$ for its ordinary right derived direct images on abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $\mathcal P$ be the class of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism] in $\mathcal C$, and let $\mathcal A'_X\subset\mathrm{Ab}(B_X)$ be the full subcategory of sheaves isomorphic to $\pi_X^{-1}F$ for torsion abelian sheaves $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Then each $\mathcal A'_X$ is a weak Serre subcategory: it contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects, and extensions. Moreover the following five properties hold.

(1) For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$ and any $Y'\to Y$, the fibre product $X\times_Y Y'$ exists and $X\times_Y Y'\to Y'$ belongs to $\mathcal P$.

(2) For every $f:X\to Y$, the restriction functor $f_{\mathrm{Et}}^{-1}$ sends $\mathcal A'_Y$ into $\mathcal A'_X$.

(3) For every $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$, its underlying presheaf on $\mathrm{Sch}/X$ satisfies the ph sheaf condition.

(4) For every $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$, every $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$, and every $i\geq0$, one has $R^if_{\mathrm{Et},*}H'\in\mathcal A'_Y$.

(5) Every ph covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ admits a refinement $\{W_{jk}\to U\}_{j\in J,k\in K_j}$ factoring through an etale covering $\{V_j\to U\}_{j\in J}$, singleton ph coverings $\{W_j\to V_j\}$ whose morphisms lie in $\mathcal P$, and etale coverings $\{W_{jk}\to W_j\}_{k\in K_j}$. Here refinement means that each composite $W_{jk}\to U$ factors through one of the $U_i\to U$. All the covering families are small in the chosen universe; torsion requires no common annihilator and no invertibility of torsion orders.

proof.text: First record explicitly that torsion small etale sheaves contain zero and are closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions. A section of a kernel is a section of the source, so its local annihilator also annihilates it in the kernel. A section of a cokernel locally lifts to the target of the original map, since an epimorphism of abelian sheaves is locally surjective; a local annihilator of that lift kills its image. For an extension $0\to F\to E\to F'\to0$ and $e\in E(U)$, first refine $U$ until an integer $n>0$ kills the image of $e$ in $F'$. Then $ne$ is a section of the kernel, identified with $F$; refine again and choose $m>0$ killing this section. Thus $mn$ kills $e$. These coverings and integers may depend on the section; no uniform bound is used. Closure under isomorphism is immediate from the same definition.

source.place: Tag 0F0I, lemma-compare-ph-etale, first proof paragraph, torsion closure implicit in conditions (1)-(4) of the weak Serre criterion.

proof.text: Fix $X$ and put $L=\pi_X^{-1}$ and $R=\pi_{X,*}$. Both are exact: $L$ by exactness of inverse image for a morphism of sites, and $R$ by the exact-retraction lemma. The latter also gives the unit $F\xrightarrow{\sim}RL F$. The adjunction therefore identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(LF,LF')$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(F,RL F')=\operatorname{Hom}(F,F')$. Every morphism between objects of $\mathcal A'_X$ consequently comes, after their chosen isomorphisms, from a small-etale morphism $u:F\to F'$. Exactness gives $\ker(Lu)=L\ker(u)$ and $\operatorname{coker}(Lu)=L\operatorname{coker}(u)$. Step 1 shows the small sheaves on the right are torsion. Exactness also sends zero to zero. This proves zero, isomorphism, kernel and cokernel closure.

source.place: Tag 0F0I, lemma-compare-ph-etale, first proof paragraph, conditions (1)-(3).

proof.text: Given $0\to LF\to H\to LF'\to0$ with $F,F'$ torsion, exact $R$ and the unit isomorphisms give $0\to F\to RH\to F'\to0$. Step 1 makes $RH$ torsion. Apply exact $L$ to this row, and map the resulting short exact sequence to the original one using the adjunction counit $LR\to\mathrm{id}$. Naturality gives the commutative diagram. Its endpoint maps $LRLF\to LF$ and $LRLF'\to LF'$ are isomorphisms: by the triangle identity they are inverse to $L$ applied to the respective unit isomorphisms. The short five lemma now makes the middle counit $LRH\to H$ an isomorphism. Thus $H\cong L(RH)$ lies in $\mathcal A'_X$, proving extension closure and the weak Serre assertion.

source.place: Tag 0F0I, lemma-compare-ph-etale, first proof paragraph, condition (4); the counit diagram fills the omitted justification of G=pi^{-1}pi_*G.

proof.text: For a proper $f:X\to Y$ and arbitrary $Y'\to Y$, the fibre product $X\times_Y Y'$ exists by the scheme fibre-product statement. Properness is stable under this base change, by the cited proper-base-change lemma. The induced structure map to $S$ makes the fibre product an object of $\mathrm{Sch}/S$. This is property (1).

For $H'\cong\pi_Y^{-1}F$, the small/big pullback formula gives $f_{\mathrm{Et}}^{-1}H'\cong\pi_X^{-1}f_s^{-1}F$ for every $f:X\to Y$. The small pullback $f_s^{-1}F$ is torsion: at each geometric point its stalk is a stalk of $F$, by the inverse-image stalk isomorphism. The local definition of torsion is equivalent to every stalk element having a positive annihilator: one implication takes germs; for the other, represent a germ by a section and shrink its pointed etale neighbourhood until the annihilating equality holds, then let the geometric point vary. The resulting etale neighbourhoods cover. This proves (2), with no restriction on $f$.

Let $H=\pi_X^{-1}F$, and let $a:U\to X$ and $p:V\to U$ be any proper surjection. Set $G=a_s^{-1}F$ on $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Evaluation of $H$ identifies $H(U)$, $H(V)$ and $H(V\times_UV)$ with the sections of $G$, $p_s^{-1}G$ and $q_s^{-1}G$, respectively, where $q:V\times_UV\to U$. Naturality in that formula identifies both arrows with pullback along the two projections. The proper-surjection section-equalizer lemma therefore proves that $H(U)\to H(V)\rightrightarrows H(V\times_UV)$ is an equalizer. This uses no torsion hypothesis on $F$.

source.place: Tag 0F0I, lemma-compare-ph-etale, A-sheaf paragraph, reducing 0DDW to its proper-surjection equalizer.

proof.text: We verify ph gluing rather than treating a tag as a proof. The affine standard-sieve basis also says etale coverings are ph, which is the asserted topology comparison. (a) Separatedness for every ph covering $\{Y_l\to Y\}$ of every object $Y$: choose an affine open cover $\{Y'_j\to Y\}$; by the basis lemma the pulled-back sieve on $Y'_j$ contains a proper surjection $W'_j\to Y'_j$ with a finite affine open cover $\{W'_{jk}\}$ whose members factor through some $Y_l$. A section of $H(Y)$ restricting to zero on all $Y_l$ restricts to zero on all $W'_{jk}$, hence on $W'_j$ (Zariski separatedness), hence on $Y'_j$ (injectivity in Step 6), hence on $Y$. (b) Let $\{U_i\to U\}$ be ph covering and $s_i\in H(U_i)$ matching. Choose an affine open cover $\{V_j\to U\}$ and, as in (a), $W_j\to V_j$ proper surjective with finite affine open cover $\{W_{jk}\}$ and maps $W_{jk}\to U_{i(k)}$ over $U$. The pullbacks $s_{i(k)}|_{W_{jk}}$ agree on $W_{jk}\cap W_{jl}$, which maps to $U_{i(k)}\times_UU_{i(l)}$; the etale sheaf condition glues them to $t_j\in H(W_j)$. Its two pullbacks to $W_j\times_{V_j}W_j$ agree on each open $W_{jk}\times_{V_j}W_{jl}$ by the same matching, hence agree. Step 6 descends $t_j$ to $v_j\in H(V_j)$. (c) $v_j=s_i$ on $Y=U_i\times_UV_j$: the family $\{W_{jk}\times_UU_i\to Y\}_k$ is a ph covering (base change of the composite covering $\{W_{jk}\to V_j\}$, site axioms), and on $W_{jk}\times_UU_i$ both sections are pullbacks of $s_{i(k)}$ and $s_i$, which match; apply (a). (d) On $V_j\times_UV_{j'}$, $v_j$ and $v_{j'}$ both restrict to $s_i$ on the ph covering by the $U_i\times_UV_j\times_UV_{j'}$, by (c); so they agree by (a), and glue to $v\in H(U)$. By (c), $v|_{U_i}$ and $s_i$ agree on the Zariski cover $\{U_i\times_UV_j\}_j$, so $v|_{U_i}=s_i$; uniqueness is (a). Thus $H$ is a ph sheaf, and so is every presheaf isomorphic to it, giving (3).

source.place: Tag 0F0I, lemma-compare-ph-etale, A-sheaf paragraph; 0DDW and topologies.tex 0DBQ, with the overlap and uniqueness details written out.

proof.text:
For proper $f:X\to Y$ and $H'\cong\pi_X^{-1}F$ with $F$ torsion, apply the proper derived small/big comparison to $K=F[0]$. Taking degree $i$ gives
$$R^if_{\mathrm{Et},*}H'\cong\pi_Y^{-1}(R^if_{s,*}F).$$
Indeed $\pi_Y^{-1}$ is exact, so it preserves the kernels, images and cokernels in the formula $H^i=\ker d^i/\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$. The degree-$i$ cohomology of a derived direct image of $F[0]$ is its ordinary $R^i$, by definition. A proper map is quasi-compact because it is of finite type, and quasi-separated because it is separated. Apply the existing qcqs higher-image theorem with the set of all primes. Its input is exactly elementwise torsion of the geometric stalks of $F$, equivalent to the local torsion definition by the germ argument of Step 5; its output says that $R^if_{s,*}F$ is torsion. Therefore the displayed big sheaf lies in $\mathcal A'_Y$ for every $i\geq0$. This is (4), including $i=0$.

source.place: Tag 0F0I, lemma-compare-ph-etale, A-and-P paragraph: 0DDJ(2) and 0DDD, keeping the qcqs hypotheses explicit.

proof.text: For (5), take an affine open cover $\{V_j\to U\}$. Pull back the sieve generated by the given ph covering to each $V_j$. The affine standard-sieve basis supplies a proper surjection $W_j\to V_j$ and a finite affine open covering $\{W_{jk}\to W_j\}$ whose composites belong to that sieve. Membership means precisely that the composite $W_{jk}\to U$ factors through one of the original $U_i$; thus the required refinement maps exist. Both open covers are etale by the basis lemma. Each singleton $\{W_j\to V_j\}$ is ph covering directly from the generating definition of the ph topology, and its arrow is proper. Composition of these three covering levels is a covering, by the site axioms. The chosen presentations and basis lemma make all index sets small; $J$ need not be finite. For empty $U$ one may take $J=\varnothing$. This proves all of (5).

split_report.summary: Proved the weak Serre assertion and all five comparison properties in nine steps along Stacks 0F0I. Reused exact small/big retraction, proper base-change stability, local epimorphism lifting, short five lemma, inverse-image stalks and the more general prime-support torsion higher-image node. Four new independent tools state small/big evaluation, proper derived small/big comparison, proper-surjection section descent and the affine standard ph-sieve basis. The counit and matching-family gluing details are explicit. No statement change and no SGA route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NY-e2f9e1357 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 0F0I (with its whole proof) against 0EZ3. The item statement matches: proper morphisms, A'_X = pi_X^{-1} of torsion abelian sheaves on X_et with no common annihilator, ordinary abelian coefficients, relocalization f_Et, and the five properties for tau=ph and tau'=etale. They match word for word the hypotheses of the consumer lem-trf-refined-topology-comparison-vanishing. The statement is unchanged and not weakened. I checked steps 1-6 and 8-9 against their cited statements: local torsion closure, full faithfulness from the unit isomorphism, the counit/short-five argument for extensions, proper base change, the 021I(3) square with stalk-germ torsion, the 0DDW reduction to the small-site equalizer, 0DDJ(2) on F[0] together with proper => qcqs and 0DDD with all primes, and the standard-ph refinement for property (5). The four new nodes are true, statement-only, correctly sourced and not duplicates: 09XN+021I(3) evaluation; 0DDJ(2) with the canonical base-change map; the 0DDW/0A3T equalizer for any abelian G; the 0DBD/0DBF/0DBI/0DBQ standard-sieve basis. I tested them on small cases: empty U, p=id, a non-surjective p (excluded), and m=0. My searches of the DAG and of blueprint main-20261015 found no duplicate. I accept the tool_uses lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact, lem-sbc-qcqs-higher-images-prime-torsion and lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective. There is no SGA citation and no cycle. FIX: step 7's uniqueness bookkeeping was out of order. It applied a separatedness check over V_j x_U V_j' that presupposed v_j = s_i on U_i x_U V_j, which was never proved. I rewrote it as (a) separatedness for every ph covering, (b) the construction of v_j, (c) v_j = s_i via the ph covering {W_jk x_U U_i}, and (d) agreement, gluing and uniqueness. I also added def-trf-ph-scheme-site to the step's uses. The corrected item JSON is in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
